set.body:
Why
For sufficiently large fused or tiled workloads, memory bandwidth and multiple cores can matter more than scalar loop quality. Parallelism can also destroy small-array latency, determinism, and JavaScript portability, so it must be explicit and stage-gated.

Scope
- Add a typed execution policy with Serial as the stable default and an explicitly selected bounded parallel JVM policy.
- Partition only general tiles or fused programs large enough to amortize scheduling. Use bounded reusable pools or structured runtime facilities; never create threads per operation.
- Preserve exception behavior, alias safety, output ownership, and deterministic completion. Reductions must use a canonical merge tree compatible with the existing exact pairwise contract or remain serial.
- Establish workload thresholds across element count, bytes, operation intensity, layout, and core count. No benchmark-name or fixture-shape dispatch.

Scala.js impact
Node and browser execution remain serial by default and must use the identical semantic API and results. Scala.js Workers are excluded from automatic promotion: transfer, structured-clone, SharedArrayBuffer, isolation headers, and startup costs require a separate design and receipt. A future Worker provider may be proposed only if large-workload evidence clears those costs. Shared policy plumbing must add negligible overhead to the serial typed-array loop.

Acceptance
- Large eligible JVM workloads demonstrate at least 1.50x end-to-end speedup on more than one core count, while small and medium serial cases stay within 10 percent of baseline.
- Results are deterministic across repeated schedules; exact reductions remain bit-for-bit compatible or are explicitly ineligible.
- Pool lifetime, cancellation, exceptions, and nested use are tested.
- Full-linked Node proves the serial fallback has no material regression and identical signatures.
- JVM and Scala.js laws, fullLink, browser correctness, and API compatibility pass.
set.title: Add an explicit deterministic parallel execution policy
